Quick update from runtime/serving side — we did push a canary rollout for model-redwood-v3-quant at 15:10 PT to 10% of Hosted API traffic as part of the scheduled variant upgrades (rollout id: roll-2026-02-26-17). Initial telemetry looked fine in the synthetic canary.

However, live traffic showed a change in request-size distribution and sequence lengths for Zenith's endpoints which triggered an unfavorable kernel selection path in the quantized runtime leading to a high-latency execution path for some sequences. We're seeing p95 jump from ~180ms to ~1.1s and p99 to ~1.7s for their key route. No increase in errors, but a latency tail.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll back canary to the previous variant (model-redwood-v3) for their tenancy (fastest).
- Apply per-tenant routing rule to pin Zenith to the older runtime path while we patch kernel heuristic (takes ~2-3 hours for patch + verification).
- Expand canary to 50% temporarily to gather more signal (not recommended while customer is degraded).

I recommend rolling back Zenith's traffic to model-redwood-v3 now and opening an internal incident to fix the kernel selection heuristic. Will prepare traces and the p95 digest.

Attaching initial trace bundle and p95 digest.

Attachment: p95-digest-20260226.csv (text/csv)

—Dev

Sam/Aarthi — thank you for flagging and for the traces. We have identified a likely regression tied to a canary variant swap (model-redwood-v3-quant). Dev is recommending a targeted rollback for your tenancy immediately, which we will do now.

Planned immediate action (ETA: 15 minutes):
- Pin Zenith traffic to model-redwood-v3 (pre-quant variant) while we investigate kernel heuristics.
- Monitor p95/p99 for the next hour and share a SLO snapshot.

We are prioritizing this and will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix. Apologies for the disruption — we understand this impacts your pilot and will keep you updated every 30 minutes until resolved.

Vanessa Ortiz

Rolled back Zenith tenant to model-redwood-v3 at 17:48 PT. Early indicators show p95 trending back to baseline — attaching the SLO snapshot and the consolidated p95 csv for the affected window. Post-rollback p95 is ~210ms; p99 ~350ms. No data loss.

Next steps:
- Assign a small bug to runtime team to adjust the kernel selection heuristic for quantized variant under long-sequence loads.
- Add a per-tenant canary guard to prevent automatic ratio-based routing when sequence distribution diverges significantly.
- Proactive outreach to other affected customers (if any) — run the same queries against canary telemetry.

Sam/Aarthi — final update from our side this morning. We rolled back your tenancy to the previous model variant and the p95/p99 have returned to expected ranges (see attached SLO snapshot and p95 digest).

What we did: 
- Immediate: performed tenant-scoped rollback at 17:48 PT on 2026-02-26.
- Short-term: implemented a routing guard to prevent mismatched kernel selection for your traffic while we validate the quantized runtime fix.
- Next: runtime team will deliver a kernel-heuristic patch and we will schedule a private canary with Zenith for verification (post-patch) to avoid a broad canary A/B that could surface regressions.

We appreciate your patience and will coordinate a short technical review call if helpful. If you need a formal RCA or an executive escalation package for your stakeholders, please let me know and we will prioritize.
